transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-11 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Recording: Fireflies auto | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM) — Derek (CISO), Lena (SRE), Priya (Compliance), Markus (Cloud Ops), Samir (Procurement)

Summary: QBR-style security and resilience review focused on KMS/encryption, data residency controls, IR + BCDR (RTO/RPO), and SLA/escalation flows. Customer provided current targets and constraints; Redwood clarified Dedicated/VPC options, envelope encryption, and audit log retention. Agreed to follow up with SOC 2 artifacts, architecture diagrams, and schedule a tabletop drill.

Topics: SOC 2 evidence, SSO/RBAC mapping, KMS & HSM options, envelope/encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs & retention, RTO/RPO targets for core inference endpoints, failover plan across regions, escalation phone tree and on-call rotations, SLA credits and notification thresholds.

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): All right everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we'll run through 45ish mins of content, leave time for Qs. Is that still good?
[00:12] Derek (CISO): Yep that's fine. We're particularly keen to review the KMS story and the incident escalation — want to make sure we can walk these up to our board.
[00:20] Avery: Great. Marco from our SE team will go deep on key management and failover. Nina will coordinate followups.
[00:30] Marco (Redwood SE): Hi everyone. Quick orient: we'll cover encryption at rest, envelope flow with customer-managed keys, HSM integration, audit log retention, then move into IR/BCDR — RTO/RPO tradeoffs for Dedicated pools versus hosted.

[02:15] Lena (SRE): Before that, two constraints — Northern Utilities must keep keys in our AWS "GovCloud-like" partitions for OH and MN, and RTO target for customer-facing inference is 5 minutes for primary endpoints and 30 minutes for batch jobs. RPO for stateful caches is 1 minute.
[02:42] Marco: Got it. When you say "GovCloud-like", are you able to confirm it's strict region isolation or do you allow cross-region replicas under encryption?
[02:55] Derek: Strict — keys must be resident in approved regions, replication between regions is allowed only if keys remain under our control.

[03:20] Marco: OK, that maps to Redwood Private or a dedicated VPC deployment with a customer-managed KMS in those regions. Our envelope encryption can be configured so the root DEKs (data encryption keys) are wrapped by your CMKs. Keys never leave your KMS for unwrapped operations.
[03:45] Priya (Compliance): And for SOC 2, we'll need key rotation docs and proof of separation of duties — who signs off on rotations, access controls, and how audit logs are retained. What retention windows are available?
[04:05] Marco: Audit log retention is configurable; hosted tiers default to 90 days, Dedicated/Private can be extended — we have 1 year, 3 year options, and transfers to your log archive. We can stream all access events (encryption API calls, service config changes) to your SIEM.

[05:10] Samir (Procurement): From a commercial side, if we ask for extended retention there's a cost delta?
[05:18] Avery: Yes typically a retention add-on. We'll include cost buckets in the follow-up.

[06:00] [interrupt, crosstalk] Markus (Cloud Ops): Quick technical: how do you handle KV cache state if a node fails mid-generation? What's the RPO there?
[06:12] Marco: Good question. For low-latency streaming endpoints we replicate KV cache across warm peers with asynchronous replication. That gives us effective RPO of ~1 minute under our warm pool configs; for stronger guarantees we can do synchronous replication at cost of added latency.

[07:30] Lena: So to meet our 1 minute RPO for caches, asynchronous warm replication is acceptable?
[07:36] Marco: Yes, that's the usual pattern. We'll propose exact warm-pool sizing.

[08:05] Derek: Talk me through the escalation tree — if we get a P1 outage that impacts critical metros, how are we notified and what's the expected time to Redwood acknowledgement and then to first action?
[08:22] Nina (Redwood CSM): Standard SLA notifications: phone + pager to customer on-call if configured, email + slack alerts. For Dedicated customers we provide a 15 minute acknowledgement SLO and for enterprise we often include 10 minute. We can adjust for contract.
[08:45] Avery: And we'll include a postmortem and follow AP when incident qualifies. Our incident response playbook maps notification thresholds to action owners.

[09:30] Derek: Our procurement will want those times as contractual obligations — can we get a formal escalation matrix?
[09:38] Avery: Absolutely, we'll include it in the compliance pack.

[10:00] Marco: On the KMS/HSM side: two paths — 1) Redwood-managed keys where we manage DEKs and you have strict IAM controls and key rotation reports, or 2) Customer-managed keys (CMK) in your KMS — AWS KMS/HSM or partner HSM — we only ever see wrapped keys. For regulatory posture you'd likely pick option 2.
[10:25] Priya: We need HSM-backed keys. Can Redwood accept an external HSM and do key ops without exporting?
[10:33] Marco: We support HSM-backed CMKs and can perform operations that accept wrapped keys; Redwood services call the KMS endpoints in your account via VPC endpoints. We never export plaintext keys. There is a small latency penalty for each wrap/unwrap call — typically sub 10ms per call but it accumulates on high QPS workloads.

[11:10] Markus: That latency is important for us. For streaming gen at high QPS we can't add more than ~5ms. Can you cache unwrapped DEKs locally?
[11:20] Marco: Yes — we cache DEKs in secure memory in the runtime and rotate them on schedule. The DEK is unwrapped in the SEV realm and cached; ops for heavy workloads only call KMS on rotation or key creation. That pattern keeps per-token latency minimal.

[12:00] Lena: Ok good. Next: SOC 2 evidence — what artifacts will you provide?
[12:10] Avery: We'll share the SOC 2 Type II report summary, control mappings, and our last auditor letter. Also a runbook extract for incident response, and the KMS architecture diagram Marco mentioned.
[12:22] Priya: Will the SOC report include details on subcontractors and third-party datastores? We need subservice organization lists.
[12:30] Avery: Yes, the SOC includes subservice lists. We'll redact customer names as needed.

[13:40] [transcription glitch] Speaker 2: — uh — if we look at the SLAs, if you offer 99.95% uptime, what's the credit model?
[13:50] Avery: Standard is pro rata credits for monthly downtime beyond threshold; for Dedicated we can negotiate enhanced SLAs and financials. We'll include sample credit tables.

[14:30] Derek: For the warm-failover plan — can Redwood automate failover between regions while preserving data residency constraints?
[14:40] Marco: We can. We support policy-driven routing that respects region and key residency. For example, if a region goes down we can failover to a compatible model in an approved region provided the CMK is available there (or you allow a wrapped-dek transfer). If your keys must remain in region A, cross-region failover requires either a pre-provisioned CMK in region B under your control or pre-warmed Dedicated capacity in region A.

[16:05] Lena: So pre-warmed capacity in region A is the safer option if keys cannot leave the region. What's the cost implication?
[16:14] Avery: Pre-warmed Dedicated pools incur reserved cost; we'll detail cost/benefit in the follow-up.

[17:00] Priya: Regarding audit logs — we need immutable logs for 7 years for compliance. Is that doable?
[17:10] Marco: Yes. We can stream logs to your S3/GCS archive with server-side immutability and object lock or to your SIEM. That solves long-term retention. There is storage cost.

[17:55] Derek: On incident response — do you have a runbook template we can align with and do tabletop exercises?
[18:03] Nina: Yes, we have an IR playbook that maps detection -> triage -> containment -> recovery -> RCA, plus communication templates. We run tabletop drills with customers; typical cadence is quarterly for critical customers.

[19:15] Lena: Can Redwood share a sample P1 runbook now?
[19:22] Marco: We'll attach the P1 runbook to the follow-up packet. It includes contact trees, run states, and play-by-play checklists.

[20:00] Derek: RTOs — you said earlier Dedicated acknowledgement is 15 mins. For first action, can you commit to 30 minutes to begin mitigation for P1?
[20:10] Avery: We can propose 30 minutes for first mitigation for dedicated SLAs; we'll put that in the proposed SLA language.

[20:55] [noise] Markus: Another ops question — how do you handle multi-tenant logs? Are they separated by account and namespace so we can provide least privilege?
[21:06] Marco: Logs are partitioned by account and customer-id; access is RBAC-controlled. For Dedicated we can provide dedicated log pipelines.

[22:30] Priya: SSO and RBAC mapping — can we integrate with our Okta? We need SCIM for provisioning and group-based mapping to RBAC roles.
[22:40] Avery: Yes, we support SAML SSO with Okta and SCIM provisioning. We'll include a role mapping doc example.

[23:50] Derek: And auditability — can you produce immutable audit trail for key unwrap ops and who initiated them?
[23:58] Marco: Yes — every KMS API call, who called it, and the user agent is logged; we can include extra context like request ID and session token. We sign logs and can route to your SIEM.

[25:00] Lena: On disaster recovery testing: what do your tests look like? Are they destructive? Do you provide a runbook before exercises?
[25:12] Nina: We provide non-destructive tabletop first, then can do live failover tests in a scheduled maintenance window. We'll supply a test plan and rollback plan.

[26:50] Derek: If we do a live failover test that involves rekeying or bringing up capacity in a second region, what's the expected downtime?
[27:02] Marco: If pre-warmed, failover is often metadata switch + routing update — typically under 2-5 minutes for stateless endpoints. For stateful caches it depends on replication settings; we can hit your 5 minute SLO with warm peers. Rekeying is slower so we pre-provision keys to avoid rekeying on failover.

[28:40] Priya: Who on Redwood's side is on the escalation chain? We need names and 24/7 contacts for legal/security notices.
[28:48] Avery: We'll provide a contact matrix: AE, CSM, SE lead, SRE on-call, and an executive on-call for P0s. We'll include phone, secondary email, and Slack escalation channel.

[30:00] [brief pause] Samir: Contractually, will Redwood accept a clause about notification timeframes and periodic tabletop obligations?
[30:08] Avery: We can accept operational SLAs and commit to quarterly tabletop drills for enterprise plans. Contract language will be proposed by legal; we'll share sample clauses.

[31:20] Marco: One more technical detail: we use signed attestations when mounting customer keys in secure enclaves; that gives cryptographic proof of key usage and non-export.
[31:32] Derek: Good. We need the exact attest artifact format so our auditors can validate.
[31:36] Marco: We'll include an example attestation with the follow-up.

[33:00] Lena: We've had historical concerns around stale feature flags causing incidents — can Redwood provide guardrails?
[33:08] Nina: We have feature-flags with kill switches and circuit breakers per route and we can add per-account safe defaults. We also have canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model to preserve availability.

[34:20] Derek: Can automatic fallback be disabled? For compliance we might prefer deterministic failure rather than degraded AI results.
[34:30] Marco: It's configurable per route. You can choose strict failure, degraded fallback, or queued mode.

[35:50] Priya: Regarding data residency logs — we need proof that data didn't transit undesired regions. Can you provide traceroute-like evidence?
[35:58] Marco: We can provide request trace logs with region tags and edge ingress points; full network traces are harder but we can show hop-level metadata and signed headers showing region-specific processing.

[37:10] Derek: OK. Let's talk about a real incident scenario — say a region outage that takes down us-east-1 and our backups are in us-west-2 but keys are restricted to us-east-1. Walk through the steps.
[37:22] Marco: Step 1: detection — automated monitors. Step 2: acknowledge within SLA. Step 3: if keys can't be used in us-west-2 then either failover to pre-warmed capacity in us-east-1 (if available) or bring up a warm standby that uses a pre-provisioned CMK in us-west-2 under your control. Step 4: contact tree and customer confirmation for cross-region rekeying if required. Step 5: RCA and postmortem. We'll draft that scenario in the runbook.

[39:00] [people murmur about scheduling]
[39:20] Nina: We'll also include a checklist of preconditions required for each failover type — e.g., key availability, warm pool size, DNS TTLs, and client-side retries.

[40:10] Lena: For telemetry, can we get token-level cost/latency breakdowns so we can see economic impact during outages?
[40:18] Avery: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and cost attributions. We'll include a sample dashboard.

[41:00] Derek: How do we prove compliance with data deletion requests? Auditors want an export of deletion attestations.

[41:09] Marco: We track deletion operations and write deletion attestations into audit logs; we can provide a signed deletion proof with timestamp and request ID.

[42:20] Priya: For the tabletop drill, can we run a scenario with rekey + failover + SLA dispute? We want to exercise legal+security+ops.
[42:30] Nina: Absolutely — we'll script a multi-team tabletop. We'll propose a date in the next 3 weeks.

[43:50] [small side conversation, unclear]
[44:10] Avery: Quick recap of concrete deliverables: SOC 2 artifacts, KMS diagram and HSM options, proposed RTO/RPO for dedicated warm-pool configs, escalation matrix and runbook extract, and pricing for extended log retention and pre-warmed capacity.
[44:36] Derek: That covers it for us. Thank you.

[44:50] Lena: Two follow-up asks — include sample legal SLA clauses and the sample auditor attestation format.
[44:58] Avery: Will do.

[45:10] Marco: One last note — on the small chance you want a hybrid where Redwood manages the runtime but keys are entirely in your HSM, we have reference architecture that minimizes latency. We'll include that.

[46:00] Derek: Great. We'll review and get back with availability for the tabletop.

[46:20] Samir: Procurement will review the cost buckets, look for the retention costs and the pre-warm reserved pricing.

[47:00] Avery: Thank you everyone. We'll follow up with the package by Tue/Apr 13.
[47:08] [meeting end small chatter]

Meeting close: quick recap and thanks.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels, minor mis-hearings (e.g., "DEK" rendered as "deck" in one short segment), and punctuation artifacts from auto-transcript.

References shared: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2-typeii (SOC 2 pack), https://redwood.ai/architecture/kms-envelope (KMS envelope diagram), sample-runbook.pdf (internal link will be attached in follow-up).

End of transcript.
